item.text:
**Assessment**
Mixed, slightly positive on crisis-response capacity, but with serious negative evidence in Papua and coercive policing. Jokowi’s government did take some concrete steps to reduce suffering during health and cyber shocks and sent humanitarian aid abroad, but it did not consistently protect vulnerable people from state violence or fully prevent harm in conflict settings.

**Claims**
- [President Jokowi Sends Off Humanitarian Aid for Palestinians, Sudanese](https://setkab.go.id/en/president-jokowi-sends-off-humanitarian-aid-for-palestinians-sudanese/) — Sekretariat Kabinet Republik Indonesia, 2024-04-03. Claim: Jokowi framed the shipment as a humanitarian mission for civilians suffering in Gaza and Sudan, which is direct evidence of trying to reduce suffering during conflict-driven crises. IDs: 6B.6; also 6B.1, 6B.3.
- [Indonesia and WHO launch collaborative surveillance to strengthen detection, preparedness, response, and resilience](https://www.who.int/indonesia/news-room/item/30-07-2024-indonesia-takes-decisive--pioneering-action-to-strengthen-multisource-collaborative-surveillance-for-dengue) — WHO Indonesia, 2024-07-30. Claim: Indonesia and WHO launched dengue surveillance to improve detection, preparedness, response, and resilience, showing active crisis-prevention and mitigation capacity in a public-health shock. IDs: 6B.6; also 6B.5, 6B.2.
- [Indonesia ramps up capacities to detect and respond to outbreaks of emerging and epidemic-prone diseases](https://www.who.int/indonesia/news-room/item/30-08-2024-indonesia-ramps-up-capacities-to-detect-and-respond-to-outbreaks-of-emerging-and-epidemic-prone-diseases) — WHO Indonesia, 2024-08-30. Claim: The Ministry of Health and WHO trained rapid-response teams in 514 districts for early detection, verification, field investigation, risk assessment, and outbreak response, which is strong evidence of practical crisis-mitigation systems. IDs: 6B.6; also 6B.5, 6B.2.
- [Indonesia's health coverage country profile](https://www.who.int/about/accountability/results/who-results-report-2024-2025/country-profile/2024/indonesia) — World Health Organization, 2024. Claim: WHO says Indonesia had high coverage, lower out-of-pocket costs, and better access to essential services regardless of gender, age, or disability, which indicates some structural capacity to cushion health-related suffering. IDs: 6B.6; also 6B.2, 6B.3.
- [Jokowi orders audit of Indonesia’s data centres after cyberattack](https://www.scmp.com/news/asia/southeast-asia/article/3268495/jokowi-orders-audit-indonesias-data-centres-after-cyberattack) — Reuters via South China Morning Post, 2024-06-28. Claim: After a major ransomware attack disrupted public services, Jokowi ordered an audit of government data centres rather than denying the failure, which is a concrete corrective response to a service-disrupting shock. IDs: 6B.6; also 6B.5.
- [President urges BPKP to audit national data center governance](https://en.antaranews.com/news/317175/president-urges-bpkp-to-audit-national-data-center-governance) — ANTARA News, 2024-06-28. Claim: The government publicly acknowledged the cyber failure and moved to audit governance, supporting a read of honest crisis correction rather than concealment. IDs: 6B.6; also 6B.5.
- [Indonesia’s tax agency probes alleged personal data breach](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/indonesias-tax-agency-probes-alleged-personal-data-breach-3622634) — Reuters via Investing.com, 2024-09-19. Claim: The alleged NPWP breach shows continuing state vulnerability, but the government did move to investigate and mitigate, so this is mixed evidence: response existed, but the underlying exposure remained severe. IDs: 6B.6; also 6B.5.
- [Indonesia says need for mitigation on NPWP data leak](https://www.antaranews.com/berita/4345027/presiden-jokowi-minta-perlunya-mitigasi-soal-kebocoran-data-npwp) — ANTARA News, 2024-09-19. Claim: Jokowi ordered rapid mitigation involving Kominfo, Finance, and BSSN after the alleged data leak, which is evidence of active crisis management. IDs: 6B.6; also 6B.5.
- [Indonesia sees no significant human-rights improvement in 2024](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128570.html) — U.S. Department of State, published 2025-08-12; report covers 2024. Claim: The report says violence between government forces and separatists continued in Papua, with arbitrary killings, torture, arbitrary detention, and weak accountability; this is strong negative evidence that the state did not consistently reduce avoidable suffering in a domestic conflict zone. IDs: 6B.6; also 6B.3, 6B.4.
- [Indonesia racism/discrimination against Indigenous Papuans](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/18/indonesia-racism-discrimination-against-indigenous-papuans) — Human Rights Watch, 2024-09-18. Claim: HRW says Indigenous Papuans faced discrimination, arbitrary arrest, torture, extrajudicial killings, and forced displacement with weak accountability, which is strong evidence against a suffering-reduction claim for a major vulnerable group. IDs: 6B.6; also 6B.3.
- [Protests across Indonesia as parliament delays change to election law](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/protests-across-indonesia-as-parliament-delays-change-to-election-law-3582501) — Reuters via Investing.com, 2024-08-22. Claim: Security forces used tear gas and water cannon against protesters during the election-law crisis, which shows that crisis management sometimes relied on coercive force that can deepen suffering. IDs: 6B.6; also 6B.3, 4B.6.
- [Indonesia’s dwindling middle class seen dimming economic outlook](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/indonesias-dwindling-middle-class-seen-dimming-economic-outlook-3610865) — Reuters via Investing.com, 2024-09-11. Claim: Reuters reported layoffs and fewer job opportunities squeezing the middle class, which is negative evidence that macro stability did not fully prevent avoidable economic hardship. IDs: 6B.6; also 5B.9, 5B.10.

**Search gap**
I found stronger evidence on health emergencies, cyber shocks, Papua conflict, and external humanitarian aid than on classic disaster or famine response inside Indonesia itself. Direct 2024 evidence for earthquake/flood/food-crisis relief was limited in the available material, so this note leans on the best documented crisis channels rather than claiming a complete emergency-management record.
